name: Raja Ahmad Shah
role: Mahmud’s son and commander in Brown’s account
bio: Ahmad’s messengers bring pressing requests for carts and boats. He can offer a court seal, but the quay still wants to know whose instructions will stand.
notes: fact: Brown presents Ahmad as reigning and rallying the bridge defense; Pires instead includes the king’s son among those opposing peace. Both report his later death at his father’s order (Brown chs. XXII–XXIII, pp. 166–170; Pires II, p. 280)
inference: Birch’s Alaoadim in a later correspondence episode is not a secure alternate name for Ahmad (Birch III, pp. 143–144; Brown ch. XXIII, pp. 170–171)
gameplay: His requisitions may compete with booked trade; they do not represent a permanent anti-trade policy (people-factions.md §§2–3)
